cleanIntro: The AUG comes apart into its major groups by hand, with no tools: barrel out the front, receiver and bolt carrier out of the stock, gas regulator off the barrel. Steyr stops the owner at the component groups and says so plainly — past that point it is factory work.

steps.title: Ammunition out of the area first
steps.action: Before the rifle is touched, empty every magazine and clear live ammunition off the bench. Steyr asks for the area, not just the rifle — a bullpup puts the chamber behind your hand, and a loose round on the mat is how a stripped rifle gets fed by accident.
steps.caution: Always wear safety glasses when disassembling your STEYR
steps.quote: Unload all magazines and remove all live ammunition from
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — STEYR AUG A3 M1 — Owner's Manual, STEYR AUG A3 M1 — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed — Chapter 6: Disassembly, opening warning, p.26

steps.title: Let it cool before you start
steps.action: If it has just been fired, give it time. The barrel comes off by hand on this rifle and you take hold of it directly — there is no handguard between you and it.
steps.aside: prevent burns from hot components, such as the barrel.
steps.quote: Be sure to allow your STEYR AUG to cool after firing it to
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — STEYR AUG A3 M1 — Owner's Manual, STEYR AUG A3 M1 — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed — Chapter 6: Disassembly, warning, p.26

steps.title: Magazine released and drawn down out of the well
steps.action: Hold the pistol grip with your right hand, finger off the trigger and outside the guard. With the magazine in your left hand, press the back of the magazine release up with your left thumb and pull the magazine down and out.
steps.quote: Pull the magazine down and out of the magazine well with your left hand;
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — STEYR AUG A3 M1 — Owner's Manual, STEYR AUG A3 M1 — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed — Chapter 6: Disassembly, steps 1-2, p.27

steps.title: Cocking slide back palm-up, locked open, chamber checked
steps.action: Pull the cocking slide back with your left palm facing up — Steyr is specific about the hand position, because anything mounted on the receiver rail is exactly where your knuckles would otherwise go. Lock it open by turning it clockwise onto the indentation in the receiver, then look and feel in the chamber. The last-round hold-open is not a check.
steps.caution: Always pull the cocking slide back with your palm facing up
steps.quote: With your left hand, with your palm facing up, pull the cocking slide back to eject any cartridge that may be in the chamber and lock it in the rear position by turning it clockwise and allowing it to rest on the indentation on the receiver;
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — STEYR AUG A3 M1 — Owner's Manual, STEYR AUG A3 M1 — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed — Chapter 6: Disassembly, step 3, p.27

steps.title: Barrel lock pin down, barrel turned and pushed forward out
steps.action: Take the barrel grip in your left hand, push the barrel lock pin button down with your left thumb, and turn the barrel grip clockwise while pushing the barrel forward out of the receiver. This is the AUG's whole character — the barrel is a hand-removable unit, no tools.
steps.quote: Hold the barrel grip with your left hand and use the thumb of your left hand to push the button of the barrel lock pin down, while turning the barrel grip clockwise and pushing the barrel forward and out of the receiver;
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — STEYR AUG A3 M1 — Owner's Manual, STEYR AUG A3 M1 — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed — Chapter 6: Disassembly, step 5, p.28

steps.title: Cocking slide returned forward
steps.action: Turn the cocking slide counter-clockwise off its indentation with your left thumb and let it run forward. It has to be off the lock before the receiver will come out of the stock.
steps.quote: Move the cocking slide forward by turning it counterclockwise with the thumb of your left hand;
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — STEYR AUG A3 M1 — Owner's Manual, STEYR AUG A3 M1 — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed — Chapter 6: Disassembly, step 6, p.28

steps.title: Receiver lock pushed across, receiver and carrier out of the stock
steps.action: Hold the top of the stock in your left hand and push the receiver lock from left to right with your right thumb, then draw the receiver and bolt carrier forward out of the stock together.
steps.aside: Pull the receiver and bolt carrier forward and out of the stock;
steps.quote: Hold the top of the stock with your left hand push the receiver lock from left to right with the thumb of your right hand;
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — STEYR AUG A3 M1 — Owner's Manual, STEYR AUG A3 M1 — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed — Chapter 6: Disassembly, step 7, p.28

steps.title: Bolt carrier drawn forward out of the receiver
steps.action: Hold the receiver in your left hand and pull the bolt carrier forward out of it with your right. That is the rifle in its main groups.
steps.quote: Hold the receiver in your left hand and pull the bolt carrier forward and out of it with your right hand;
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — STEYR AUG A3 M1 — Owner's Manual, STEYR AUG A3 M1 — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed — Chapter 6: Disassembly, step 9, p.29

steps.title: Gas regulator pressed and turned out
steps.action: Hold the barrel, press the pressure piece of the gas regulator in and turn it clockwise until its slot lines up with the nose of the gas cylinder, then take the regulator out. This is where an AUG's fouling actually collects.
steps.quote: Press the pressure piece of the gas regulator in, while turning it clockwise until its slot is in the same position as the nose of the gas cylinder;
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — STEYR AUG A3 M1 — Owner's Manual, STEYR AUG A3 M1 — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed — Chapter 6: Disassembly, gas operating system, step 2, p.30

steps.title: Stripped to its groups — and that is Steyr's limit
steps.action: The rifle is now in its major component groups: barrel, receiver with bolt carrier, stock with trigger mechanism, magazine and the gas parts. Steyr stops here in plain words — anything past this is factory work.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — STEYR AUG A3 M1 — Owner's Manual, STEYR AUG A3 M1 — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed — Chapter 6: Disassembly, closing instruction, p.37
steps.warn: Never further disassemble your STEYR AUG. Any further disassembly must be performed by STEYR authorized personnel.

deepAbsentReason: Steyr publishes the field strip above and then stops in plain words: the rifle is never to be disassembled further, and any further disassembly must be performed by Steyr authorized personnel. There is no bolt, firing pin, extractor or trigger-mechanism teardown anywhere in the 43 pages — the trigger mechanism comes out of the stock as a sealed unit and is not opened. That is the manufacturer's published DON'T and it stands; nothing deeper was invented from it.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Brush the bore from the chamber end and patch it dry, then leave a light film
Clean the chamber and the locking recesses
The barrel is off the gun — clean it as a separate part, which is the advantage

cleaning.name: GAS SYSTEM
tasks: Clean the gas regulator and the gas cylinder nose where carbon builds
Check the regulator turns freely and its slot indexes cleanly before it goes back
Do not oil the gas parts heavily — oil there bakes into carbon

cleaning.name: BOLT CARRIER & RECEIVER
tasks: Wipe the bolt carrier, its guide rods and the bolt face
Clean the receiver interior and the rails the carrier rides on
Lubricate the main parts lightly after firing, per Steyr's maintenance chapter

cleaning.name: STOCK & TRIGGER MECHANISM
tasks: Wipe the stock interior out; a bullpup collects debris where the trigger group sits
Wipe the trigger mechanism housing exterior — do not disassemble it
Keep cleaning solvent off the polymer and out of unventilated areas

reassembly: Chapter 8 of Steyr's manual is a full reassembly procedure — it is the disassembly reversed, in order.
Trigger mechanism back into the stock, retaining bolt in, butt plate on.
Bolt carrier into the receiver, then receiver and carrier back into the stock until the receiver lock seats.
Gas regulator back in and turned until it locks.
Barrel in through the front of the receiver, turned counter-clockwise until the barrel lock pin springs up and captures it — check it is locked before anything else.
Cycle the cocking slide and confirm the action runs before the magazine goes near it.
fncheck: With the rifle confirmed empty and no magazine fitted, check the barrel is locked in (it should not turn or draw forward), cycle the cocking slide and confirm the bolt carrier runs fully forward into battery, and check the safety crosses over positively before the rifle is stored or carried.
